## Purpose

`apps/scan/src/` is a flat folder of 17 `.rs` files, one per stage of the pipeline (ingest, extract, graph, mine, condense) plus the projections (`digest`, `facts`, `spec`, `rank`, `pagerank`) and the shared vocabulary (`model`, `matching`, `manifests`, `classify`, `dictionary`, `stemmers`). There is no `lib.rs`, no subdirectory and no re-export facade: every module is declared in the `mod` list at the top of `main.rs` and reached module-qualified as `crate::<module>::…` (the digest calls `crate::classify::anchor_eligible` directly rather than wrapping it locally). Each module is a small set of free functions over borrowed data, not an object graph. The engine stays blind: everything that names a language, build system, tool, marker or natural language is DATA in a sibling catalog at the crate root, embedded at compile time. Output must be byte-stable on any machine, which drives every container and sort choice below.

## Convention

- File: `apps/scan/src/<stage>.rs`, lowercase single word naming the responsibility. Add the `mod <stage>;` line to `main.rs`.
- Header: a `//!` module doc that states the ONE responsibility and the rationale — why the stage runs where it runs, what its determinism and tolerance contract is, and the measured verdict behind a contested choice. `dictionary.rs` carries `## Why this is a SCAN STAGE, not a projection`, `## Two sources, one corpus` and `## Determinism` sections; `classify.rs` states its probe order and its tolerance rule up front. This doc is the design record, not decoration.
- Public surface: free functions, usually one entry point named `build` (`condense::build_skeleton`, `dictionary::build`, `facts::build`, `digest::build`) taking borrowed slices/maps and returning an owned value. Helpers are private `fn`; only what another module actually calls is `pub(crate) fn` (`facts::owned_manifests`, `digest::tokenize`, `digest::stopwords`).
- Knowledge lives outside `src/`: a crate-root `*.toml` (`stopwords.toml`, `generated-markers.toml`, `manifests.toml`, `ranking.toml`, `languages.toml`), `stoplists/*.txt`, or `queries/<dir>/*.scm`. Load it once with a `OnceLock` plus `include_str!` — see `classify::catalog` and `manifests::registry`. Adding a language, build system or marker is a data row, never a new branch.
- Determinism: `BTreeMap` / `BTreeSet` for anything whose iteration reaches the output; `HashMap` only for internal lookups that are never iterated into a result. Every sort carries an explicit tie-break (`b.count.cmp(&a.count).then(a.affix.cmp(&b.affix))`). Scores are integers, x1024 fixed point, so no float ever enters a comparison.
- Tuning values are file-top `const`s with a doc-comment justifying the number (`MIN_COUNT`, `MAX_ANCHORS`, `MAX_TERMS`, the per-query caps), never inline literals buried in a loop.
- Tolerance: a catalog row or pattern that fails to compile is dropped individually, an unreadable input yields an empty result, and the scan never panics or aborts. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside `#[cfg(test)]`; the single production `expect` sits on an embedded catalog that ships inside the binary (`digest::stopwords`).
- Model evolution is additive: fields on `model.rs` types carry `#[serde(default)]` (plus `skip_serializing_if` when absent is the common case) so an older `grain.model.json` keeps deserialising.
- Tests: unit rules go in an inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the bottom of the same file, with tiny local builders and `..Default::default()` for the rest. End-to-end contracts go in `apps/scan/tests/<topic>.rs`, over a fixture tree in `apps/scan/tests/fixtures/<name>/`, spawning `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_scan")`.

## How to apply

A new responsibility becomes a new flat file `apps/scan/src/<stage>.rs` plus one `mod <stage>;` line in `main.rs` — never a subfolder, never a `lib.rs`, never a wrapper that re-exports another module's function. Decide first whether it is a scan STAGE or a PROJECTION: a stage runs inside `analyze()` in `main.rs` because it needs data that only exists during the scan (the in-memory `content` map with the comments — the reason `dictionary` is a stage), and it is wired into the `analyze` sequence; a projection takes `&ProjectModel` and nothing else, and must never touch the filesystem or re-read the repo. Write the `//!` doc before the code, stating the responsibility and the determinism/tolerance contract. Keep the entry point a `pub fn` over borrowed inputs returning an owned value, put every threshold in a documented `const`, and keep every name that a grammar, language or tool would recognise out of the file — put it in a sibling catalog and read it through `OnceLock` plus `include_str!`. Close with an inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` proving the rule you just encoded, and add a `tests/<topic>.rs` case when the behaviour is only observable through the produced JSON.

## Examples

- Ref: `apps/scan/src/classify.rs` — catalog-driven engine: probe order documented in the header, `OnceLock` + `include_str!`, module-qualified policy functions consumed by the digest, tolerance on bad rows.
- Ref: `apps/scan/src/dictionary.rs` — the long-form stage doc (why stage, not projection), documented `const` caps, `BTreeMap`/`BTreeSet` throughout, and two inline `#[cfg(test)]` modules.
- Ref: `apps/scan/src/condense.rs` — the minimal end of the same shape: two-line header, one `pub fn build_skeleton` over borrowed input, `BTreeMap` accumulation, explicit sort and truncate.
- Ref: `apps/scan/src/facts.rs` — `pub fn build(model)` projection plus `pub(crate)` helpers shared with `main.rs`, with the unit tests inline at the bottom.
